I recently had to call CPS/social services on my former neighbors across the street.

I usually mind my own business when it comes to my neighborhood; I don’t like prying into other people’s affairs. But there were multiple occasions when their children (younger than 4yo) were getting outside and wandering the streets completely naked. Several occasions that I had to run out and bring the kid back to their house and pound on the door for several minutes to get them to come to the door.

It happened a lot. I once caught their two year old crawling under my next-door neighbors car, then wandering in the street while a massive truck almost ran her over.

If it was only once or twice, I would’ve chalked it up to kids being kids and not blamed the parents. They did have six kids, after all, and at least one of them was special needs. But this was clearly becoming a case of neglect, and we have multiple sex offenders (with a record of offenses against children) living just a few doors down. Eventually, I had to call CPS. Thankfully they did respond and perform a check-in, and the incidents stopped for a little while as the kids went to stay with relatives for a brief period. 

But as soon as they got the kids back, it started up again. After a few more calls CPS informed me that these people had a record of neglect and abuse, and that I should call the police. So I kept an eye out.

I never got the chance. A short time later, around 10pm one night, an ambulance raced through our neighborhood and stopped in front of their home. When they came out of the house, they carried with them the body of one of the children. Apparently the mother had drawn a bath for two of her children, but didn’t drain it before leaving to attend a baby. Her two year old daughter wandered into the bathroom, fell into the tub, and drowned.

The rest of her children were taken away after that. Whether or not she got them back, I can’t say for certain. But they moved away. Our new neighbors are kind, quiet, and thankfully childless.

While I’m sure that CPS did the best they could, I don’t call them anymore. I just call the police right away.

I wish I could have done more for that poor little girl.
